question.value: How the millimeter/submillimeter flux of the gamma-ray binary B1259 changes around the 2024 periastron passage, and what this implies for the pulsar wind and the circumstellar disk

findings_qualitative.value: Band 3 flux rises about tenfold toward periastron, consistent with synchrotron emission from shock-accelerated electrons

evidence.quote: This is a tenfold increase from pre-periastron levels.
consistent with synchrotron radiation from shock-accelerated electrons in the pulsar-stellar wind interaction

findings_qualitative.value: Band 6 and 7 spectra rise with frequency away from periastron, indicating thermal emission from the circumstellar disk; synchrotron dominates Band 6 only near t_p ~ -1 day

evidence.quote: the synchrotron emission becomes dominant at periastron ($t_p\sim -1$ days), whereas the thermal emission is the dominant emission mechanism at other phases

findings_qualitative.value: Band 7 brightening after periastron suggests the disk survives the pulsar passage and may have expanded

evidence.quote: The post-periastron brightening in Band 7 (343 GHz) indicates the resilience of the circumstellar disk and possible expansion of the disk.

claims.hypothesis: Does the Band 3 emission near periastron come from synchrotron emission produced by the pulsar-wind interaction?
claims.experiment: Band 3 (97 GHz) observations at t_p = -61, -28, -1 and +29 days
claims.result: Flux rises from low early values to 3.17 +/- 0.20 mJy at t_p = -1 day, then falls to 1.34 +/- 0.10 mJy at +29 days
claims.finding: The Band 3 emission near periastron is synchrotron from relativistic electrons accelerated in the pulsar wind and stellar wind or disk interaction

evidence.quote: suggesting synchrotron emission from relativistic electrons
Strong variability in the Band 3 (97 GHz) emission, peaking near periastron

claims.hypothesis: Does the dominant mechanism at Band 6 change between thermal disk emission and synchrotron around periastron?
claims.experiment: Band 6 (233 GHz) observations at -61, -31, -1 and +29 days and SEDs against Band 3 and Band 7
claims.result: Spectrum inverts between Bands 3 and 6 near periastron with alpha ~ -0.3, less steep than typical synchrotron (-0.75); Band 6 decays more slowly after periastron
claims.finding: Synchrotron dominates at Band 6 near periastron, while thermal disk emission dominates at other phases, with possible disk contribution even at periastron

evidence.quote: which could indicate a contribution of the disk emission to the Band 6 emission
A more complex behavior in Band 6 (233 GHz), suggesting a transition between synchrotron and thermal emission mechanisms

claims.hypothesis: Is the circumstellar disk destroyed by the pulsar passage?
claims.experiment: Band 7 (343 GHz) observations at -57 and +24 days compared with 2017 and 2019 Band 7 data and a thermal disk model
claims.result: Band 7 flux at +24 days is 3.11 +/- 0.54 mJy, higher than before periastron; model disk size grows from ~20-30 R_star to ~40 R_star
claims.finding: The disk is not immediately destroyed and may have expanded, possibly through the pulsar wind pushing the disk outward

evidence.quote: suggests that the circumstellar disk remains largely intact despite the pulsar’s close approach
the brightening in Band 7 may be due to the effect of pulsar winds pushing the disk outward

why_this_data.value: ALMA allows study of emission above ~100 GHz with excellent sensitivity, and earlier mm data only covered other orbital phases; new data target behaviour around periastron

evidence.quote: The advent of the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) allowed us to study the emission at higher frequencies ($\gtrsim 100$ GHz) with excellent sensitivity.
These observations were aimed at capturing for the first time the behavior of the system around the periastron passage.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Tidal interaction alone as the cause of the Band 7 post-periastron brightening was judged insufficient

evidence.quote: However, even taking this into account, it would be difficult to explain the 2-fold brightening by tidal interactions alone.

limitations_admitted.value: Few ALMA epochs, so the double-peaked light curve seen at low frequencies cannot be tested

evidence.quote: We note that since the number of our ALMA observations is small, the double peaks found in the light curves for the low frequency radio and X-ray bands
despite fewer data points

limitations_admitted.value: The flux at a given orbital phase can vary from one orbital period to the next

evidence.quote: although the flux at a given $t_p$ can vary for each orbital period

referee_caveats_inferred: Only 1-2 epochs in Band 7 and at most four per band, so claims on disk expansion and the thermal-to-synchrotron transition rest on very few points
Flux errors in Table 1 are not tied to a stated measurement method and absolute flux-scale uncertainty is not discussed
Different array configurations give very different beams (0.11'' to 2''), and the paper does not discuss possible resolved-out disk emission or beam-dependent flux
Disk size estimates from a literature thermal model are given without model parameters or fit quality
Light curve comparison mixes different orbital cycles (2017, 2019, 2024), which the paper admits vary cycle to cycle

missing_for_reproduction: Flux extraction method and error budget
Full CLEAN parameters, spectral window selection and mask
Target position, calibrator flux models, and mapping of project codes to epochs
Parameters of the thermal disk model and of the synchrotron/pulsar components overplotted in the SEDs
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: About 10 short (5-6 min) observations in three bands; raw data likely a few to tens of GB, pipeline products smaller
reproducibility.score_reason: ALMA project codes and per-epoch fluxes are given, and calibration and robust are stated, but flux measurement, CLEAN details, target coordinates and the disk model are not specified
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Flux extraction and SED/disk-model recipe are underspecified, and the public status of the 2023.1.00271.S data is not stated in the paper
